skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

3. // The MicroVM platform's guest-virtual -> guest-physical translation map.
4. //
5. // MicroVM runs the guest identity-mapped, so the abstract map is the identity
6. // over the entire usize address space. This is a platform-level invariant (the

8. // the translation on MicroVM must still yield the identity, so the equality is
9. // part of the contract, hence `open`.
10. //
11. // Total: defined for every address. Deterministic: a function of `gva` alone.
12. // Frame correspondence (the caller's load-bearing property) and injectivity are
13. // immediate corollaries of this identity.

8.   module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
9.   Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
10.   `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
11.   state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
12.   the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
13. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
14. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
15. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
16. - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
17.   `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
18.   op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
19.   region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
20.   the abstract `bump_view`.
21. - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
22.   `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
23.   `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.
24. 
25. ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
26. 
27. - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
28.   page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
29.   Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
30.   volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
31.   `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
32.   `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
33.   carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
34.   PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
35.   `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
36.   change).
37. - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
38.   page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
39.   Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
40.   `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
41.   `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
42.   index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
43.   contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
44.   `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
45.   `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
46.   slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
47.   **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
48.   `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.
49. 
50. ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)
51. 
52. - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
53.   `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
54.   entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
55.   verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
56.   page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
57.   `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
58.   `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
59.   state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
60.   so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
61.   `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
62.   This matches the inherited upstream
63.   `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
64.   `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
65.   `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

77.   `nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`). Body cannot be verified; `ensures` states that, on `Ok`,
78.   every frame in `phys_regions_frame_set(&physical_memory_regions)` becomes reserved.
79. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same `LinkedList` limitation.
80.   `ensures` states that, on `Ok`, every *covered* frame in `mmio_regions_frame_set(mmio_regions)`
81.   becomes reserved (uncovered MMIO frames are skipped, matching the `frame::is_covered` gate).
82.

85. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init` — also listed under skip; callable from verified `init`.

87. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::Upool` (struct) and `Upool::new` — no specs yet; opaque

90.   paths call. `ensures` describes the free→allocated transition (`alloc_one`) and the empty-pool

 ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
 
 - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
   page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
   Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
   volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
   `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
   `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
   carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
   PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
   `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
   change).
 - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
   page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
   Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
   `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
   `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
   index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
   contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
   `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
   `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
   slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
   **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
   `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.
 
 ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)
 
 - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
   `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
   entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
   verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
   page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
   `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
   `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
   state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
   so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
   `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
   This matches the inherited upstream
   `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
   `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
   `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

   spec_kernel_watermark()` ties the runtime value to the abstract spec value. The companion spec
